reasoning: Recent data specific to Massachusetts focuses heavily on the 2026 U.S. Senate race rather than the presidential contest, and within that, mostly on the Democratic primary rather than general‑election matchups.[2][3][4][6][7][15] A compiled general‑election polling average from Pollsmax for the Massachusetts Senate race shows Democrat Ed Markey leading Republican John Deaton by roughly D+23 in the current aggregate, indicating a very strong Democratic advantage in the statewide Senate environment.[2] I did not find any credible, state‑specific Massachusetts presidential general‑election polling within the last 45 days, so the best current numeric read is that the Senate race is strongly D‑favored by about the low‑to‑mid‑20s in margin, with structural conditions (PVI D+14) also strongly Democratic.[9]

sources.name: Pollsmax
sources.details: Pollsmax’s Massachusetts Senate 2026 general‑election polling average has Ed Markey at 54.1% and John Deaton at 31.0%, an overall Democratic lead of D+23.1 based on seven aggregated polls.
sources.date_range: various (average current as of August 17, 2026; underlying polls mostly June 2026)

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (via Pollsmax aggregation)
sources.details: UNH Survey Center’s Massachusetts poll cited here found Markey leading Deaton 50% to 34% in a general‑election matchup, a D+16 margin incorporated in the broader Pollsmax average.

sources.name: UMass Amherst / WCVB (reported by GBH)
sources.details: A UMass Amherst/WCVB statewide poll of registered voters found Ed Markey leading Seth Moulton 60% to 32% among Democratic primary voters, a D+28 advantage within the primary electorate rather than the general.

sources.name: UMass Amherst / WCVB (reported by WBUR)
sources.details: WBUR’s coverage of the UMass Amherst/WCVB poll similarly reports Markey at 60% and Moulton at 32% in the Democratic Senate primary, confirming a sizable D+28 lead among Democratic primary voters.

sources.name: UMass Amherst / WCVB (reported by Boston.com)
sources.details: Boston.com’s write‑up of the UMass Amherst/WCVB poll reiterates that Markey holds 60% to Moulton’s 32% among Democratic primary voters, emphasizing his strength across demographic groups.

sources.name: UNH Survey Center (summarized by PredictionHunt)
sources.details: PredictionHunt summarizes a UNH Survey Center poll showing Markey leading Moulton 41% to 35% (D+6) in the Democratic Senate primary, an earlier, tighter primary snapshot rather than a general‑election measure.

sources.name: Unnamed July Democratic primary poll (reported by PredictionHunt)
sources.details: A July survey described by PredictionHunt shows Markey leading Moulton 41% to 35% with a large undecided bloc, again measuring only the Democratic primary rather than the statewide general election.

sources.name: Suffolk University / Boston Globe
sources.details: A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll cited by the Globe found Markey leading among younger Democratic voters in the Senate primary; it describes age‑cohort primary preferences rather than a general‑election margin.

sources.name: UMass Amherst / WCVB and UNH (reported by WAMC)
sources.details: WAMC’s report on the UMass/WCVB poll notes Markey leading Moulton 60%-32% in August 2026 and contrasts it with a June UNH poll where Markey led 41%-35%, both reflecting Democratic primary dynamics rather than the general.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Cook Partisan Voting Index (statewide figure via summary)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index, as summarized here, lists Massachusetts with a statewide PVI of D+14, indicating the state has voted roughly 14 points more Democratic than the national average in recent presidential elections.
sources.date_range: 2020 & 2024 presidential elections (basis for index, published August 13, 2026)
